title: DNF Rate and Book-Abandon Patterns
dataSources: Reading progress (`reading:progress`), highlights (`highlight:capture`), note links (`note:link`), books finished (`book:finished`).
app: Reading and knowledge-management telemetry — Goodreads / StoryGraph libraries, Kindle highlights (Readwise), and note-graph exports (Obsidian, Notion) — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=reading:progress
| stats sum(eval(if(status="abandoned",1,0))) as dnf, count as started by genre
| eval dnf_rate=round(100*dnf/started,1)
| where started>=3
| sort - dnf_rate
description: Tracks which genres you most often abandon partway, revealing where your taste and the hype diverge.
value: A did-not-finish pattern helps you stop buying books you predictably will not finish, saving money and guilt.
implementation: Ingest reading outcomes into `index=personal`; compute abandon rate by genre.
visualization: Bar chart of did-not-finish rate by genre.
grandmaExplanation: It shows which kinds of books you tend to give up on, so you buy fewer you will not finish.
